title: Fall of Troy
summary: CFAH AP-12: the destruction of Troy (1184/1183 BC), the end of the Trojan War.
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Sorted by the CFAH anchor point cited below; Herodotus entries are display only.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 3: Anchor Points of Ancient History," ARJ 16 (2023): 131–154, section "AP-12: The Fall of Troy: 1184/1183 B.C."
chronologies.note: CFAH-3: "Four hundred and eight years added to 776/775 B.C. yields 1184/1183 B.C. for the fall of Troy." Eratosthenes is taken as the most reliable witness.

chronologies.date: “it was not just to come upon them for what Proteus, king of Egypt, was detaining”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.118 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 144 (PDF p. 146)
chronologies.note: Synchronism: in the priests' story Proteus held Helen in Egypt during the Trojan War (2.112–120).

chronologies.date: “to the time of Pan, son of Penelope (Pan, according to the Greeks, was her child by Mercury), is a shorter space than to the Trojan war, eight hundred years or thereabouts”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.145 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 159 (PDF p. 161)
chronologies.note: Pan about 800 years before Herodotus, and the Trojan War earlier than that. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): 450 BC + 800 = about 1250 BC, so the Trojan War falls before about 1250 BC. Anchor: CFAH-3 dates Herodotus's visit to Egypt to 450 B.C. (section "Conflicting Information: Herodotus Nine Centuries Below Moeris"; AP-21). CONFLICT (about 66 years or more): CFAH AP-12 dates the fall of Troy 1184/1183 BC, later than Herodotus's implied date. The sentence is loose ("or thereabouts").
